newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks climb to third straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks climb to third straight record close.

text.p: The Mexican stock market notched up its third record close in a row on Thursday, boosted by Wall Street's powerful rally and foreign buying ahead of the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday.
The blue-chip IPC share index ended up 32.39 points, or 0.71 percent, to an all-time closing high of 4,591.62, after climbing as high as 4,622.41 points in morning trade.
"The bourse ran out of fuel once Wall Street closed, on top of which we saw some profit-taking," said Hector Jimenez, a technical analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
"The market climbed on the outlook for lower interest rates, stronger economic indicators and a flood of foreign investors," said Raul Ochoa, an analyst at Inverlat.
Volume was heavy, with 120.4 million shares changing hands, reflecting a strong inflow of foreign capital.
Ochoa said Mexican stocks remained in demand after rising sharply recently, because they were still undervalued compared with shares on other regional equity markets.
"The IPC is still below record levels in dollar terms, which still makes it attractive to foreign investors, as we can see in demand for (Mexican) ADRs," he said.

Market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) ended 16 centavos (2 cents) higher at 19.70 pesos ($2.47), a record in peso terms. Telmex American Depositary Receipts ended up 3/8 at 49-3/4, a high for the year but still well short of their all-time peak of 74 reached in February 1994.
The Dow Jones industrial average finished 100.43 points higher at a record 7,895.81 in an abbreviated trading session prior to the Fourth of July U.S. holiday on Friday.

Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, was the most active issue. Its B shares gained 7 centavos (1 cent) to 4.07 pesos (51 cents) as lower domestic and international interest rates suggested problems with past-due loans might ease, traders said.
Paper company Kimberly Clark de Mexico, in which Kimberly-Clark Corp has a minority stake, gained 0.80 pesos (10 cents) to 32.60 pesos ($4.09).
Dealers said brighter prospects for the company's second-quarter earnings lured foreign buyers, after the stock had considerably lagged the market.
On the broad market, gainers outnumbered decliners by 65 to 37, out of 124 stocks that changed hands.
Textile firm Hilasal gained 20 centavos (2.5 cents) to 3.20 pesos (40 cents), ending near the top of the percentage gainers list after Caspian Research initiated coverage of the stock with buy.
